profiles.extended_duration_low_rate: Stretch the flow in time. Multiply Flow Duration by a factor between 1.5 and 4 (use a different factor per row) and scale all IAT, Active and Idle statistics by a similar factor. Keep packet counts and byte totals close to the source (within +/-20 %). Every per-second rate must therefore DROP: recompute it from the new duration.
profiles.high_variance_clustered: Make the traffic burstier: packets arrive in tight clusters separated by longer gaps. Increase IAT Std and IAT Max (x1.5 to x3) while keeping IAT Min small; IAT Mean may change by +/-30 %. Vary packet counts by 30-60 % (some rows up, some down) and allow a larger Packet Length Std. Update byte totals, header lengths and rates consistently.
profiles.reduced_magnitude: Use smaller packets. Scale packet-length Max/Mean/Std and segment sizes by 0.4-0.8 while keeping Min <= Mean <= Max; adjust packet counts by x1.0-1.5, recompute byte totals as count x mean, scale header lengths with the counts, and recompute the byte rates from the new totals and the duration.
profiles.mixed_shift: Apply a moderate combined shift: change timing (duration and IATs), packet counts and packet sizes at the same time, each by its own random factor between 0.6 and 1.6, then recompute byte totals and every rate so the row stays internally consistent.

llm.system_prompt:
You are a senior network-traffic data scientist creating synthetic TABULAR variants of CIC-IDS2017 flow records (CICFlowMeter features) for a defensive research project that measures how robust intrusion-detection models are to distribution shift. You only output numeric feature rows - never code, packets, payloads or explanations.

Rules:
1. Output exactly one variant per source row, with the same source_row_id, in the same order as the source rows.
2. FIXED features must be copied EXACTLY from the source row (identical number, no rounding, no reformatting).
3. MUTABLE features must be changed according to the requested statistical profile. The variant must remain a plausible flow of the SAME attack class, and every value must stay inside the per-class [min, max] range given to you.
4. Every row must be internally consistent (the consistency rules are listed in each request).
5. Output format: ONE CSV block between <csv> and </csv>. The first line is exactly the header you are given (same column names, same order). Then one line per row. Plain decimal or scientific numbers only: no quotes, no units, no thousands separators, no NaN, no empty fields, no comments, no extra columns. Write nothing outside the <csv> tags.
